title: Relative purity of a finite type scheme module family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $F$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Use the scheme relative assassin [def-trf-relative-assassin]. A specialization $a\leadsto b$ means $b\in\overline{\{a\}}$. For a morphism $v:T\to S$, write $X_T=X\times_ST$, $F_T=\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$, and $f_T:X_T\to T$ for the projection [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. An impurity above $s\in S$ is data $(v,t'\leadsto t,\xi)$ with $v(t)=s$, $\xi\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_T/T}(F_T)$, $f_T(\xi)=t'$, and $\overline{\{\xi\}}\cap (X_T)_t=\varnothing$, where $(X_T)_t$ is the scheme-theoretic fibre of $f_T$ over $t$, viewed as a subset of $X_T$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. An elementary etale neighbourhood $(T,t)\to(S,s)$ is an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] with $v(t)=s$ such that the induced map of residue fields $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism. Say that $F$ is pure along $X_s$ if there is no impurity above $s$ for which $(T,t)\to(S,s)$ is an elementary etale neighbourhood; it is pure relative to $S$ if this holds for every $s\in S$. Say that $F$ is universally pure relative to $S$ if there is no impurity above any $s$ for any morphism $T\to S$. Thus this last condition requires every relative associated point above $t'$ to have some specialization in the fibre above $t$, for every base change and specialization in that base.
